stem: An agriculture study measures crop yield across 4 regions, each containing multiple farms. region A has 15 observations with mean 70.3 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 8.9). region B has 10 observations with mean 82.4 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 8.6). region C has 10 observations with mean 48.0 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 6.4). region D has 8 observations with mean 74.3 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 3.4). The between-region standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 7.4 and 18.5 tonnes/hectare. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true crop yield for region B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-region variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for region B: 81.8 tonnes/hectare (shrunk from raw 82.4). Range [80.8, 82.1] as between-region SD varies from 7.4 to 18.5. Pooled mean: 68.7.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 68.7 tonnes/hectare (weighted average of 4 region means).
Shrinkage factor for region B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/10). At σ_between=12.3: B = 0.953.
Interval [80.8, 82.1] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (82.4) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (68.7) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
